reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that Zr migration at a coating-substrate interface improves bondability and that a gradient HfZr alloy forms, but it does not involve an HEA bond coat, thermal cycling, oxidation resistance, or spallation reduction. The key premises about the mechanism, conditions, and specific outcome are therefore largely unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Zirconium addition to an HEA bond coat will form a graded interfacial layer during processing and high-temperature exposure.
This graded layer improves adhesion by reducing thermal expansion mismatch and promoting stronger metallurgical bonding.
The graded layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, mitigating oxide scale spallation.
The mechanism is effective under high-temperature (up to ~900°C) cyclic oxidizing conditions.
The effect is specific to Zr and analogous to the behavior of Hf/Zr in related systems.
